task.title: Share tasks through a remote other than origin
task.description:
Workbook shares tasks through one remote, `origin`, and that is the repository that holds the code. This story lets a project share its tasks through a different remote, or more than one.

The reason it is scheduled now is hosting. "Run the board behind a sign-in proxy" is built and tested first with a server credential that opens the whole code repository, so a break-in on the server can read the code. Some teams cannot accept that. With this story they keep their tasks in a second repository that holds only Workbook refs, give the server a credential for that one, and the server can no longer reach the code at all.

## What is needed

- **A code checkout can share tasks through a remote other than `origin`.** Contributors keep working in their code checkout; their task changes go to, and come from, the tasks repository.
- **A repository holding only Workbook refs is a supported remote.** It has no branches and no code. "Set up a tasks-only folder with one command" already covers the server's side of this; here the contributor's side and the automatic synchronization have to work against it too.
- **A project says which remote its tasks use, once, for everyone.** A new contributor who clones the code and runs the one bootstrap command ends up pointed at the right place without being told.
- **`fetch`, `push` and `sync` can name a remote.** Each remote's tasks are kept apart under `refs/workbook/remotes/<remote>/tasks/*`.
- **Nothing changes for a team that uses only `origin`.** It stays the default and needs no configuration.
- **Moving an existing project.** A documented way to take a project whose tasks live beside the code and move them to a tasks-only repository, without losing history.
- **The hosting guide gains the second setup.** It shows the server pointed at the tasks-only repository with a credential that opens nothing else.

## Decisions

Decided 2026-11-21.

1. A project shares its tasks through exactly one remote at a time. Publishing to several at once is out of scope; nothing needs it, and it raises what happens when they disagree. The story was renamed from "Support multiple task remotes" to match.
2. The choice is recorded in the project's committed settings file, `.workbook/config.json`, which travels with the code. Every clone agrees, and an existing checkout picks up a change with an ordinary pull.
3. The tasks repository's address is stored in that same file. `workbook setup` adds it to the checkout as a second Git remote and pulls the tasks from there. A contributor can override the address locally, for example to use SSH where the file says HTTPS.
4. After a move, the task refs on the code repository are left in place and the code repository is marked as "tasks have moved". A checkout that has not picked up the change is refused with a message saying where the tasks went, so it cannot save edits to the old place unseen. The existing `refs/workbook/project` record looks like the place for the marker; confirm it can carry one when building.

How this works for a contributor, as agreed with Dylan:

- Cloning the code repository brings the settings file, which names the tasks repository.
- `workbook setup` reads it, adds the remote and pulls the tasks. From then on creating, updating, `workbook next` and the background sync all use the tasks repository. Branches, commits and pull requests still go to `origin`.
- A contributor needs push access to both repositories. One who can reach the code but not the tasks repository is told so plainly by setup, and is not left with an empty board.
- The hosted server is pointed straight at the tasks repository with a credential for that alone. It never sees the settings file or the code.
- An existing checkout learns the new address on its next pull. Proposed, to settle when building: Workbook tells the person to re-run setup, and does not add the remote on its own.

## Done when

- A project configured to share tasks through a second, tasks-only repository works end to end: an edit in a contributor's code checkout appears on a hosted board whose server can reach only the tasks repository, and an edit on the board appears in the checkout.
- With that setup, the server's credential cannot read the code repository, and the guide shows how to confirm it.
- A fresh clone of the code plus the bootstrap command reaches the tasks without manual Git steps.
- Automatic publication, `workbook next`, and `workbook sync --watch` all use the configured remote.
- A project that never configures a remote behaves exactly as it does today.
- The automated suite covers a tasks-only remote alongside a code remote, using temporary local remotes.
- The README, `docs/reference.md` and `docs/architecture.md` describe choosing a remote, and the hosting guide covers the tasks-only setup.

---

**Related finding from PR #71 (2026-08-10):** the perf harness helper deleteTrackingTaskRefs (internal/perf/scenarios.go) clears all of refs/workbook/remotes/ while the product fetch prunes only refs/workbook/remotes/origin/tasks/. Harmless while origin is the only remote (fixtures populate only the narrow prefix), but PR #71 proved this helper is load-bearing for the local-bare sync scenarios, so when multiple remotes land the two scopes must be reconciled deliberately — otherwise samples silently measure a different starting topology per remote. Align the helper scope with whatever per-remote prune semantics this story defines, or document why the harness intentionally clears wider.

comments.author: a@example.com
comments.body: Sequencing decided 2026-11-16: this now comes after "Run the board behind a sign-in proxy". Hosting is built and tested first with a server credential that can reach the whole code repository. This story then adds the option some deployments need: a second repository that holds only Workbook refs, so a hosted board's credential opens tasks and nothing else. For that it has to let a code checkout share its tasks through a remote other than origin, and treat a repository holding only Workbook refs as a supported remote.
